strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem for code representation learning and program analysis: transferring information from source code and comments into representations usable from low-level code alone.

The combination of frozen source/comment encoders, a trainable binary encoder, and learned interpolation provides an interesting, concrete approach. The figures and pseudocode communicate the overall training pipeline reasonably well.

The reported LLVM results are promising. Function-name accuracy reaches 33.41 versus 29.41 for the strongest listed baseline, and summarization BLEU-4 reaches 34.36 versus 32.43. Four downstream tasks, component ablations, and a CodeT5 extension provide useful empirical breadth.
weaknesses: Necessary: Resolve the POJ-104 evaluation protocol. Sections 3.2 and 4.2 describe 104-way classification, but Table 2 specifies disjoint sets of 64/16/24 problem labels for training/development/testing. Ordinary supervised classification does not explain evaluation on these unseen classes. Specify whether the task is retrieval, classification, or an explicit unseen-class protocol, together with its training objective and MAP/MAR/MAF1 definitions. This ambiguity prevents reliable interpretation of a central experiment.

Necessary: Align the application claims with the evaluated inputs. Section 3.1 uses compiler-generated LLVM IR, and Figures 6–8 retain meaningful identifiers and types. Such inputs are not trivially interchangeable with representations recovered from stripped executables, contrary to footnote 1. Either evaluate the claimed stripped-binary setting or explicitly restrict the findings to compiler-generated LLVM IR and document retained information.

Necessary: Strengthen attribution of improvements to interpolation and gradual training. CONTRABIN receives 30 or 70 pretraining epochs, whereas the primary-contrastive baseline receives 10. Section 5.1 asserts convergence without presenting supporting curves, and removing both interpolation stages does not establish their individual contributions. Matched-budget controls and separate stage comparisons would support these claims; otherwise, attribute improvements only to the complete training recipe. Single-seed results also leave robustness and small performance margins uncertain.

Necessary: Make the implemented objective and architecture reproducible. Equation 4 supplies raw averaged similarities as cross-entropy targets, whereas the preceding text says a softmax is applied. Specify the actual target construction, gradient treatment, similarity normalization, and loss direction. Essential projection-network and downstream decoder details are also insufficiently described, particularly for generation using encoder-only backbones.

Necessary: Clarify evaluation independence. Section 3.2 says generation performance is evaluated using the validation set, while Section 4.3 describes using the test set. Document the actual pretraining and downstream partitions, checkpoint-selection procedure, and overlap controls for the GitHub-derived corpora. The manuscript does not establish leakage, but its reporting leaves these safeguards unresolved.

Necessary: Narrow or substantiate claims about semantic correctness and comprehension. Lexical metrics and selected examples do not establish executable correctness, long-range understanding, or semantic preservation. The comments are generated by CodeT5, making independent validation and clear provenance of summarization references especially relevant. Semantic checks or independent assessment would support the stronger claims. Reverse-engineering results should also be described as mixed: GraphCodeBERT obtains higher BLEU-4, 71.56 versus 71.14.

Necessary: Correct the embedding-analysis inference in Section 4.1. Distinct programs can legitimately form semantic clusters, and fewer clusters in a t-SNE visualization do not prove better representations. Recast Figure 6 as an illustration rather than evidence establishing embedding quality.

Optional: Correct GLUE/GLEU terminology, reconcile DIRE/DIRT/DIRTY naming and citations, resolve the missing T5 references, and shorten repeated human-learning analogies. These presentation improvements are secondary to the unresolved validity and reproducibility concerns.
